items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: I found out in later years that the Captain of our station, he was somehow related to somebody, one of the Admirals here in the Twelfth Naval District so I don't know whether he had the pull or what

ctx.x: They weren’t really V-disks, because I think the V-disks were smaller. These were large glass. They ended up large glass disks, and we would go down there. We recorded two for another — what was it, the Office of War Information and something else, someone else we recorded for. So we could have done V-disks because they were very popular. I know I think the Glenn Miller overseas band I think they did V-disks, and so many of the other service bands. But with us it turned out that we were considered as a top rated…

Well they had bands all over the place you know. So they picked our band. Now I don’t know why. I found out in later years that the Captain of our station, he was somehow related to somebody, one of the Admirals here in the Twelfth Naval District so I don’t know whether he had the pull or what, but then of course we always met the challenge. Every week we’d have at least three tunes. And special arrangements. And also at that time during the war this area was one of the greatest areas for dance bands. That…
